Never inside src/. The upgrade skill already calls the releases API for its already-on-latest check. Depends on the release-practice research

What the release skill does, step by step: version scheme and bump, the log summary, the shape of the notes draft, the upgrade guidance spec, the install.sh stamp, tag and gh publish. Depends on the release-practice research and u1

How does an upgrade update Ang's own settings entries without duplicating them? The user-favouring install merge would append a changed Ang hook beside the old one (candidate: diff against the previous release's settings.json found by the recorded SHA)
What does taking only chosen parts of a release look like in the escape hatch: per file, per feature or per changelog entry, and how does the version record show a partial upgrade?

When install.sh runs in a subdirectory of a git repo, does it install at the repo root (git rev-parse --show-toplevel) or stop and ask the user to cd there? And should it warn when the working tree has uncommitted changes, so the install's changes can be reviewed on their own?

knowns.fact: Requirements and options as Zac framed them

Gitignored *.local.* files (pilot.local.md, local styles) sit physically under src/.claude/ in this repo through the symlinks. Git never ships them, but any install route that copies src/ from disk would. Keeping them out of a release is this epic's job (giget fetches from GitHub, so it holds as long as releases are cut from git)

Copy-in fits, plugin doesn't: plugins can't ship rules or permissions, wipe user edits on update and namespace skills; candidates are plain degit/giget copy-in, copy-in plus a hash-manifest update, or copier
knowns.answers: Install route: plugin marketplace, copy script or degit-style clone, given users must own and edit their copy?

knowns.fact: Copying src/ brings project-context/README.md along with .claude/, so an install gets the conventions doc without library init copying it
knowns.answers: How does project-context/README.md reach a user's install, and should library init copy it?

knowns.fact: Zac's upgrade ambition: a recorded installed version, an upgrade skill that merges upstream around local improvements, an escape hatch for oversized upgrades with pick-the-parts options, and a fast path for simple merges (the local changelog he also wanted is parked, d10)

install.sh lives at the repo root, outside src/, so the copy-in never ships it. Users pipe it from raw.githubusercontent.com/zacbraddy/ang/<ref>/install.sh to sh. The ref is stamped into the script, with an optional argument to override it. Spiked: install.sh never appears in an installed tree
knowns.answers: Where does install.sh live and how is it fetched (repo root rather than src/, URL pinned to a release tag) so it never ships into installs itself?

knowns.fact: install.sh resolves the ref to a full SHA through GitHub's API, installs that SHA and writes .claude/ang/version.json { ref, sha, installedAt }. Spiked: the record matched git rev-parse on every run
knowns.answers: Where and in what form does an install record its Ang version (tag, commit SHA), and how does an upgrade baseline an instance with no record, such as ohnvm?

knowns.fact: A file-by-file three-way merge (base: the version.json SHA; git merge-file where both changed) sorts every file into one category. Across 28 upstream-changed files and 6 local improvements, only 4 files needed judgement. Conflicted files are the cost signal; fast-path and new-file counts are nearly free. Clean merges can still be semantically stale, and upstream moves look like deletions
knowns.answers: How would an upgrade skill merge upstream changes around local improvements: what makes a merge simple versus too much (the escape hatch), and what does taking only chosen parts look like?

knowns.fact: Minimum supported Node is the current LTS (long-term support release), Node 26 today, bumped each October with engines, .node-version and CI (open-source-hygiene d11). install.sh and the documented prerequisite check for >=26, not just that node exists
knowns.answers: What minimum Node version do the documented install prerequisite and install.sh's node check state? It waits on open-source-hygiene's u7: docs say 21+, but the code's import.meta.dirname needs 22.16+. install.sh itself needs only 18+ (fetch). Once it's settled, install.sh should check the version, not just that node exists

knowns.fact: Releases are git tags with generated GitHub Releases and no hand-kept changelog (open-source-hygiene d13). Generated notes can't declare moves or migrations, so u1's answer must come from something other than a changelog

Researched: semver at 0.x (minor bump for breaking changes pre-1.0). Copy-in tools (copier _migrations, Angular ng update) keep cumulative, version-keyed migration data in the versioned tree and run every step between installed and target, and none studied reads Release bodies at upgrade time. Every mainstream release tool needs Conventional Commits, changeset files or labelled PRs, so an LLM draft fits Ang. LLM-drafted notes exist (copilot-release-notes, communique) and always need human review. No install script studied checks that a ref is a release, so Ang's tags-only check is its own. Cheap to adopt: immutable releases, a release-body skeleton with Breaking changes first, per-version guidance, draft-then-publish. Not yet worth it: CHANGELOG.md, checksums, signing
knowns.answers: How do widely used open-source projects manage releases (versioning, changelog vs release notes, upgrade and migration guides, release assets, release tooling, install scripts pinned to tags), and where would Ang's release skill depart from that convention?

decisions.decision: Install by copy-in of src/ (giget/degit --force) wrapped in a shipped install.sh, so the install is one copy-pasteable line. The script protects the user's .claude/settings.json and carries future install changes to every new user (Zac's call)

No uninstall command: removing a vanilla install is deleting skills, rules and project-context/, and local workflow improvements make automating it unreliable. Easy by hand, hard to automate (Zac's call)

The upgrade skill is in scope for this epic and is to be built. Zac's deliberate exception to the intent's build-the-least: real value, and it belongs to the same logical unit of work as install, however big it has grown

install.sh merges an existing .claude/settings.json with node (already required, no jq dependency) and first keeps a backup of the user's original, in case the merge drops properties that mattered (Zac's call)
Tests ship with installs: a local workflow improvement may change shipped scripts, and having the tests on hand lets the user run them to check (Zac's call)

giget stays, run through npx and pinned to giget@3.3.1; the README and docs list node with npm/npx as the prerequisite. Zac's call: node is already required, giget carries features we'd otherwise hand-roll, and documenting npm/npx beats also leaning on curl and tar inside the script

The install's settings merge favours the user: their values win, Ang adds only missing keys, arrays are unioned, and only the first backup (.claude/settings.json.pre-ang) is kept, so re-runs are no-ops. Spiked: the user's outputStyle, model, deny rule and hook all survived, with no duplicates on re-run

No pre-open-source upgrade path: the skill isn't designed around instances like ohnvm, because only Zac has them and only until he upgrades them. A missing version record never hard-stops an upgrade, so an LLM-run upgrade of ohnvm may succeed by accident (Zac's call)

The upgrade skill merges file by file, three-way, against the version.json SHA, with git merge-file. Fast path when no file needs judgement. Guided merge when a handful do (clean merges reread against upstream's diff, conflicts resolved with the user, conflict-deletes checked as moves). Escape hatch before writing anything when many files conflict or there's no version record. The 'many' threshold rests on two spike runs; tune it on real upgrades

No local changelog of workflow improvements in v1: diffing the instance against the version.json SHA already shows what changed locally, and the user supplies the why during a guided merge. Parked with a wake condition (Zac's call)

Cutting a release is in scope for this epic: the repeatable process (stamp the tag into install.sh, tag, publish the generated GitHub Release, plus whatever u1 settles) belongs here, since install.sh and the upgrade skill consume releases (Zac's call)

install.sh checks before copying anything and stops with a plain message saying what's wrong and how to fix it: node >=26 (k9) and npx, inside a git repo, Ang not already installed (points to upgrade), no collisions with existing project-context/ or same-named skills, rules or agents, settings.json parses, and the ref resolves (says which of network, rate limit or bad ref failed). On success it prints version, location and next step. No OS, disk or permission checks (Zac's call)

The upgrade skill checks before writing anything and stops with a plain message when: already on the target release, the target is older (downgrade), the working tree is dirty, or prerequisites are missing. A missing or unknown version record goes to the escape hatch, not a stop (d8). It finishes with a from/to, clean-vs-judgement summary and how to review (Zac's call)

install.sh and the upgrade skill install and upgrade only to published releases, never a bare SHA or branch. The default target is the latest release, and an override must name a release tag. The resolved SHA is still recorded beside the tag as the merge base. Zac raised this during the install spike, and the upgrade guidance needs it: it is written per release (Zac's call)

A release skill that lives only in the Ang repo (it doesn't ship in src/) cuts each release. It summarises the git log since the last release, drafts human-readable release notes and the upgrade guidance, edits them with Zac in a markdown draft, then stamps install.sh, tags and publishes with gh. The prose is drafted by an LLM and edited by Zac, which is what open-source-hygiene d13's 'no hand-kept changelog' meant: nothing written by hand (Zac's call)
